quest.title: The Ashen-White Order Burns
quest.description: You and Flins discover that the cannon's firing is Rerir's doing, but his motives remain a mystery. Either way, you are running out of time...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act II
chapter.title: Elegy of Dust and Lamplight

talks.objective: Return to your room to rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ergh, so much noise... What's going on this time...

dialogues.speaker: Urho
dialogues.text: Hey! Where's Flins!? Is he here, or isn't he?

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: We would be most obliged if you would pipe down a little, dear guest. Our other guests are resting...

dialogues.speaker: Urho
dialogues.text: Resting!? We're all about to be done for, and you're talking about rest!?

dialogues.speaker: Urho
dialogues.text: Flins is a Wild Hunt shapeshifter, here to deceive us all! If we don't get rid of him now, there'll be no end to this!

dialogues.speaker: Gori
dialogues.text: You'd better give him up — if anything happens, your business here is done for. You want that, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Taisto
dialogues.text: Or are you in cahoots with him? You with the Wild Hunt too, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened? Did something leak out?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we were so careful last night... How did anyone see us?

choices.text: Something fishy about this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What do you mean?

choices.text: They clearly know something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is so confusing... What do we do? These people are no match for Flins, but they're super heated right now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's not like all the unusual stuff about him will make it any easier to explain, either.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go buy some time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay!

response.speaker: Urho
response.text: Hey! Let us in, now!

response.speaker: Demyan
response.text: My apologies, my apologies.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on! Calm down, everyone!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: What in Teyvat is the meaning of this racket? Are you intent on depriving both the Voynich Guild and the Curatorium of Secrets of even a moment's rest?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Boss, do we really have to entertain people who don't respect the rules? Call a few of your boys and have them thrown out.

response.speaker: Gori
response.text: And what hole did you crawl out of?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: A watering hole, of course — the one you've just disturbed. A place to get a moment's respite from all the recent unhappiness, and to escape from all this talk of the Wild Hunt, or strange ghosts and phantoms.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Who'd have guessed people like you would come bursting in, shrieking louder than any ghoul?

response.speaker: Urho
response.text: Tch. This is a matter of utmost importance! We've got solid evidence. All we need now is to confront Flins, face-to-face!

response.speaker: Taisto
response.text: Exactly! And you sure don't look like an impartial party either, Nefer.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh, don't I now? How about this then, Boss? Let them do their search. If they find their man, they can have their little chat.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: But if they don't, then they owe everyone here an apology — as well as compensation for all the racket they've caused.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, it's... Huh?

response.speaker: Demyan
response.text: Alright, alright... I suppose that's the only way. If we don't let them in now, they'll be back sooner or later... *sigh* What a mess.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, alright then...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well? I'd say that sounds like an impartial proposal. What say you? Or are you suddenly unsure of yourselves?

response.speaker: Urho
response.text: Hmph. Come on, everyone. Move it!

response.speaker: Gori
response.text: ...No sign of Flins...

response.speaker: Taisto
response.text: B—But... How can that be? Hasn't he always stayed here!?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Done searching, are we? Guess it's time to uphold your end of the bargain, huh?

response.speaker: Urho
response.text: Waaaaaah!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After teaching the group a harsh lesson, Nefer finally lets them go. You leave the area as well.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: So, Paimon. You've been waiting to ask me something, haven't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, uhh... How did they even find us here?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: My inside man with the Lightkeepers informed me that you paid the crime scene a late-night visit. I surmised that you must have rendezvoused with Flins and obtained some new information.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Then, early this morning, a group of people gathered at the town gates, news spreading amongst them that the Wild Hunt could disguise itself by taking on familiar faces.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Everyone started throwing out the names of possible suspects — no one, seemingly, was exempt.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And amidst it all, Flins's name started gaining more and more traction. I'm sure his solitary lifestyle may have played a part, but I wouldn't discount Rerir throwing fuel on the fire in secret.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, did Flins make his escape after hearing about this?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Hehe. And that's where I — Jahoda, the quick-witted, fleet-footed backbone of the Curatorium — got my chance to shine!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: While everyone was super focused on the argument in the main hall, I alone noticed an opening—

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I got her to climb up to a window to help Flins out, only for her to return with nothing but a lantern.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: ...Aw, come on, Boss, I was just getting started!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: We initially intended to bring Flins back to the Curatorium and wait those people out, but I never expected this to be all that was left.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I imagine, though, that he wouldn't have left something that was so seemingly important to him behind.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Might he intend to come back and get it later? Maybe... I'm not sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Well, he's outta harm's way now, so that's not super important, right?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What Paimon means to say is... We've got lots of new intel to share!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Hmm... Alright then. Jahoda, contact the others. We're going to need all hands on deck.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Let's have this discussion over at my place.

choices.text: Why else would they be talking about a "Wild Hunt shapeshifter"?
I doubt it's because of anything we did.

talks.objective: Go to the "Curatorium of Secrets" to inform your companions of the new intel

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I see. So Flins has a fragment taken from within a Wild Hunt anomaly...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Is he gonna be okay now that he's on his own again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Earlier, he said that the fragment had gone still, so it's probably of no use to Rerir now.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: In that case, Rerir shouldn't have any reason to keep pursuing him, right? So was all that ruckus back at The Flagship just an act of spite, or what?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If I were him, I would have simply turned my attention to collecting other fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #A reasonable course of action. Remember what we heard back at the tavern, {NICKNAME}? The actual number of Wild Hunt anomalies destroyed has been greater than Lightkeeper records would indicate.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Some of these must have been Rerir's doing. He must have been seeking more fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This much is pretty easy to understand... But why would he pretend to be Sousi and put so much effort into getting the cannon up and running again?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Maybe 'cause that'd be more efficient than having to clear anomalies himself?

choices.text: Flins mentioned that if the cannon were fired at the Wild Hunt...

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Yeah, I'm confident that the ammo we're packing has the oomph to do that. But I am a mechanic, after all — for me, test data and their conclusions speak loudest.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Why don't we find a few of those fragments ourselves and use kuuvahki to carry out a little experiment?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Our lab could certainly accommodate such a test.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In other words, we gotta destroy a couple of anomalies and collect fragments from them, right?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Lightkeeper operations have just about ceased following the Sergeant Major's passing.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Meanwhile, the Wild Hunt continues to grow in scale by the day... I fear only we can keep the situation under control now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then we'd best act fast. Paimon's got a bad feeling about this...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: A feeling we all share, I'm afraid.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The fragments, the cannon, kuuvahki, Rerir, and the Abyss... There must be some thread linking all these factors together.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Besides, is getting revenge on Flins truly Rerir's sole aim?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We're missing some decisive connection here, but we're running out of time.)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: There are three Wild Hunt sites that must be dealt with urgently... But I believe we have the capacity to handle it.

choices.text: Since that's the case...

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Works for me. Ineffa and I will take our workshop assistants to deal with one of the sites.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The Curatorium will handle another.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: And we Frostmoon Scions shall deal with the remaining one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, Paimon didn't think she'd ever get to see everyone here carrying out a plan together like this...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Never mind you — this is a first for me, too...

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Let's head out, then. We'll meet back up at my lab with the fragments.

choices.text: If you run into Rerir, do not engage him.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Understood.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Time is of the essence now. Our foe could make his next move at any moment, so we must stay in contact with one another.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gotcha. Stay safe, everyone!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Anyone seen the lantern? Has Flins dropped by already?

choices.text: He's grown much stronger since our last encounter.
I'd like to investigate something on the Lightkeepers' end one more time.
...The fragments would be blasted into oblivion too.

talks.objective: Go to the Final Night Cemetery to meet Flins

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No one's guarding this place, just like he said. But, uh, where do we find the information he mentioned?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: This way.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Let's move. We're running out of time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, there you are! Okay, let's split up and make this happen...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Or not! How are we supposed to read through this many files!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, this might be...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Difficult, yes, but it is also our most efficient option.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: To expose the true intentions of this Rerir, we need to dive into Nod-Krai's history.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Hope we don't land on our heads, then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh! Gh—Ghost!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That file s—s—suddenly moved by itself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is a graveyard, right, Flins? D—Do these things just kinda... happen?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Many strange things happen here, but this is not one of them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: B—But that file really did m—m—move by itself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, come out! D—Don't scare Paimon like that!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I don't sense anything.)

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm? "Wild Hunt Phenomena Log"? Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, another file's moving!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: With a similar title, too...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Are we... being given hints? I feel no hostility. On the contrary — it seems we're being aided, somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? H—Hey, seriously, another one? O—Okay, then... Paimon'll read this one!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, finally finished! Paimon sure could use a long break from long words now... Hope she can remember it all.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The material I've read through has all been about past Wild Hunt incidents of enormous scale. What about you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pretty much the same here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon as well! Guess that makes three of us.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm. Whatever this is, it seems to want us to notice something. Let's bring our files together and give them another look through.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, Paimon'll go fetch hers!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, all these incidents look pretty different...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Wait, I've noticed something. Before the occurrence of these huge Wild Hunt events, a smaller-scale one would erupt in the exact same location.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: And look — all these smaller-scale Wild Hunt site reports share a common outcome.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They'd be detected, but would go inactive before any forces could be sent to deal with them. They could then be sealed directly using a Tideseal Stone... Eh, but why?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Was Rerir actively clearing these sites?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Some of these records are too old. I doubt he had regained the ability to act freely yet, or we would have met long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, and here's another similarity! "Kuuvahki in nearby soil completely drained." Could this be important, somehow?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Kuuvahki and the Wild Hunt are mutually opposed forces.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: We Lightkeepers previously believed that these small Wild Hunt sites would temporarily go inactive due to being neutralized by the kuuvahki present in the soil.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: But now that we've synthesized all this data, there is a key issue this hypothesis cannot explain...

choices.text: If the Wild Hunt's power had already been neutralized...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Indeed. Despite the name, I would not call a Tideseal Stone's sealing powers "watertight," exactly — but for it to fail and the situation to deteriorate in such short order...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Urgh... Paimon feels like she's almost got it...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Wild Hunt was not suppressed by kuuvahki. Instead, it became stronger...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (And Rerir wants to use Aino's cannon, the ammo of which is also made using kuuvahki...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Could it be—!?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He can use kuuvahki?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Yes, that might be it. It could be that when kuuvahki and Abyssal energies meet, the stronger side will suppress the weaker one.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: And while kuuvahki can indeed destroy small-scale Wild Hunt anomalies, should Rerir be strong enough... the kuuvahki might be his for the taking instead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon kinda gets where we're going with this!

choices.text: The Abyss always seeks to corrupt...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: What are you referring to?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We had a real close encounter with the Abyss in Natlan. It's a force that tries to taint everything... Ergh, it's hard to explain in detail, but basically, your reasoning makes sense!

choices.text: So Rerir also grew stronger...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Was there a gap between him pretending to be Sergeant Major Sousi and the cannon being fired?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There was! Aino needed to make some adjustments after we finished those repairs. Rerir, disguised as Sousi, left at that point...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Leaving him more than enough time to shapeshift into you, return to the Lightkeepers' office, and set up the crime scene, before heading over to the cannon's target area and absorbing the kuuvahki.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It all makes sense... And all that, just for the fragment I had with me.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It begs the question: What makes it so special that he needs it so badly?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's... still a mystery.

response.speaker: Voice from Somewhere
response.text: *knocking*

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Hmm? That's odd. We shouldn't have any guests.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I'll go take a look.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ah, it's... an ibis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's carrying a letter! Ooh, Lauma must've sent it. She can speak to little animals.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's see here...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: "Situation Urgent: The cannon began operating shortly after we left Nasha Town, and is preparing to fire."

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: "It is locked on to Starsand Shoal. Please return to Nasha Town and assist with all haste. Lauma."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's gotta be Rerir's doing! But why's he using the cannon again? Didn't he already fire it once before?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: No time for speculation. He's already made his preparations. If you recall, his body was incomplete when we last met.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: If this bombardment continues to increase his strength, he might regain his "complete" form.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A "complete" Sinner...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What should we do? There's no way we're getting back to Nasha Town in time!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll just have to trust them.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: ...Let's go to the cannon's target site. That's where we should find Rerir — and that's where we'll stop him.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: One moment, just let me get this news to Lauma. Nasha Town is in their hands now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Go, fly! Not a moment to lose!

choices.text: ...On account of the cannon being fired?
This is just like the Abyssal threat the ancient dragons faced.
...Why would another large-scale Wild Hunt occur soon after?

talks.objective: Rush to Starsand Shoal to stop Rerir

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You're here. As expected.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Humans... You never change. Always trying to use powers you neither comprehend nor control.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: But it is also thanks to you that I found a way to return.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've messed with the cannon again, huh? Sorry, but this round's not gonna go your way!

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Ah, hahaha... Such faith in your companions.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: But will the inhabitants of Nasha Town understand why they wish to stop the cannon? I think not.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: When all they see is the Wild Hunt surging up everywhere they look, the cannon must seem like their only lifeline.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: This is the truth I have revealed to them.

choices.text: So that's why you riled them all up...

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: They did this all of their own volition.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: The zealous worship of power leads only to annihilation of equally zealous proportions. True power does not heed the commands of the weak.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: You were waiting for us to leave Nasha Town, then.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: Of course. I imagine the one you call "Aino" would have managed to stop the cannon otherwise. Shame, then, that you proved one step too slow.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: In their folly, the townspeople will bar the path of all who seek to stop the cannon — and your kind-hearted, weak companions have not the stomach to deal with them. The cannon will not be stopped now.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Well, sir, you look most pleased with yourself. In that case, before you put us out of our misery, I would like to ask you a question, if I may.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: See this fragment? It once haunted your dreams, but now, it seems useless to you. What is it, exactly?

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: Hmph. That... is my corpse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: S—Sorry, what!?

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: My body was once torn into countless pieces and hurled into the swirling chaos of time itself. But even so, my life and will were not extinguished.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: Ah... Every last fragment calls to me. Sooner or later, they shall welcome my return.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you even saying...?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Huh, so the terror of the Wild Hunt was, in fact, caused by scattered pieces of your corpse... I guess they don't call you one of the Five Sinners for nothing.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: Hmph. Serendipity guided the fragments to construct an incomplete version of myself, upon which I began collecting more within Wild Hunt sites across the land...

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: But each time, the fragments I obtained were hardly worth mentioning.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: While that which you hold in your hand... was my heart.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: So that's why it responded so strongly to you.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: Only by retrieving this most critical piece could I gain mastery over the turbulent kuuvahki energies and be fully reborn.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Hence you fired that first shot hoping to regain enough power to seize the fragment from me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you completely crazy? Weren't you afraid of dying?

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: Dying? Hahaha... Such power has no hope of killing me. It may destroy my form over and over, yet always, I rebuild it. It may smash my flesh and crush my bones, thousands of times and more, but that is of no consequence to me.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: What truly infuriates me, however, is how you've destroyed my heart. All that suffering, everything I endured... and all for nothing!

choices.text: Wanna go for another round, then?

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: I have adapted to the strength and flow of this kuuvahki. The next cannon shot will multiply my strength immeasurably.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: It will not be a full restoration, no. But it will be more than enough to destroy any in this world who stand in my way.

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: Still, I suspect the kuuvahki will have rendered you down to nutrients for my consumption well before you have the time to kneel before me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Behind you... Look at that light...

choices.text: It's going to turn out the same, you know.
...You were baiting them into firing the cannon.

talks.objective: Enter Nasha Town, now in chaos
Talk to everyone in front of town

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Dang it, who fired up the cannon without my say-so!?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Its defensive barrier has also been activated, likely in anticipation of interference by malicious actors.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The air is thick with fear and anxiety... It's spooking the birds and beasts. What exactly is going on?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You're here. Looks like this was all part of Rerir's plan. Not only did he plant seeds of suspicion in people's hearts... Seems he's now igniting them.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Jahoda's gone in to scout out the situation. She'll be back any minute—

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I'm back, I'm back! Oh, it's bad out there. Rumors flying everywhere you turn... Something about the Wild Hunt preparing to spawn a wave of monsters, the likes of which we've never seen before...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...But that's not even the worst of it.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Lots of folks don't even believe the cannon can prevent this crisis, so they're getting ready to make a run for it. Others are trying to make a quick buck out of this whole mess...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: How could they still be thinking about Mora when such a catastrophe is imminent...?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Unprecedented danger brings unprecedented opportunities in its wake... A chaotic situation can bury much wrongdoing.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Even those who flee without reserve put themselves at the mercy of the divine. Is it any wonder, then, that some will aim to profit?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: After all, a gamble that might rewrite one's entire life is hard to come by.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Even so...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well, seeing as you disapprove of their actions so strongly, Lady Moonchanter, I suggest that you be the one to handle them. Not like that's the only major problem on our plate right now...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Affirmative. We must quell the chaos in Nasha Town as soon as possible. Also, the unexpected activation of the cannon entails a high risk of incorrect operation. This must be stopped in a timely manner.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Well, about that... People have been talking about how someone might come to stop the cannon. They've decided they won't let anyone in.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: What!? I made that thing! They can't just take it from me! Let me over there — what are they gonna do, stop me?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: They might, if Rerir has already formulated some countermeasure.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: For example, he might have spread a rumor that the Wild Hunt would take your form...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Possibility: High. If they view the cannon as Nasha Town's only hope, they are likely to conclude that anyone who tries to stop it must be with the Wild Hunt.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: We will face strong resistance, but they are just ordinary people. Brute force must be avoided if possible.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: There's no time. Let's go into the town. I'll find some way to calm the townspeople, you find a way to stop the cannon.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back. Mm? And you have a letter?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME} won't make it back in time, so they're heading straight over to Starsand Shoal instead.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: #Wait, what? Isn't that the cannon's target? Why would {M#he}{F#she} go there!?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Assessing Risk Level: Maximum.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: So if we can't prevent the cannon from being fired...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #Then {M#he's}{F#she's} prepared for the worst...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #And we must ensure that {M#his}{F#her} trust in us is not misplaced. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Most of those we've met so far have been attempting to escape, so they haven't gotten in our way. But it won't be so easy from here on out.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Looks like they've formed groups to protect the cannon. If they believe that we're with the Wild Hunt, we'll have no choice but to force our way through.

dialogues.speaker: Ryksa
dialogues.text: Is that... Lady Lauma? But... are you... really her?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you, Ryksa. I believe you recognize this power, having lived on Hiisi Island for so long. It is not something that anyone else could imitate.

dialogues.speaker: Ryksa
dialogues.text: I do, yes... So it really is you, my Lady.

dialogues.speaker: Ryksa
dialogues.text: But why are you here? Really, I... I believe you, but the others... Well, they'll be on high alert.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The townspeople have been misled into believing that they needed to activate the cannon. I am here to stop them.

dialogues.speaker: Ryksa
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I know what you wish to say. Our island and Nasha Town have never had close ties. There should be no reason for me to intervene.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But you chose to leave the island — you had the resolve and the courage to start a new life.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It is unfair — unjust — that you should be dragged into this mess just as that life was about to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I seek to redress this injustice, not only for you, but for everyone here who wishes to live their lives free from this chaos.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Please, have faith in our longstanding friendship... and that this is where my heart has led me.

dialogues.speaker: Ryksa
dialogues.text: ...Thank you, my Lady, thank you... Please, help us.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Then come. I need you to step forward alongside me, and to do your part too.

dialogues.speaker: Ryksa
dialogues.text: Alright. I understand!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hah, seems we chose the right person for the job. Alright, everyone — let us meet again later.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Huh? You're not coming with us?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We won't be able to calm this storm by our power alone. As such, I'll need to contact some... Let's call them friends in high places, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let's go, Jahoda.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: O—Okay...! See you again, everyone... Um, that is, if we can...

dialogues.speaker: Ryksa
dialogues.text: Lady Moonchanter, there's a child here!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It's alright now. Go, quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Thank you for bringing us here. We can quickly overcome the barrier by going upward from over there.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The cannon is all yours now.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Got it. Thanks, Lauma. Ineffa, give her a krumkake.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Orders received and immediately deferred. Departure takes priority—

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Please, everyone, listen to me.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I will not deny that we hold different beliefs, but in the face of the immense threat that hangs above us all, we must persist in trusting one another.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Otherwise, rifts will surely form, prized open by those who harbor ulterior motives.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If your fear is born of helplessness, if you flee because you know not how to fight, then follow me, you who are lost.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I am no god, but so long as we hold our candles steady and unite beneath the same moonlight, no deception or rumors can be concealed from us.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Let us resolve, then, to defend ourselves — and to stand firm against the false illusions by which our foe seeks to beguile us!

talks.objective: Try to get close to the cannon

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: This isn't good, Ineffa. We gotta hurry!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Scanning... Kuuvahki ammunition fully loaded. Preheating complete. The cannon is going through its final pre-fire checks.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: *sigh* ... Alright. Let's hit the emergency brake.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Assessment: Not enough time. Emergency brake will cause internal explosion of stored kuuvahki. Damage assessment: Incalculable. Nasha Town likely to be blasted skyward.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: No, no! I mean a manual brake. You know, the primitive kind.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: A "manual brake"... Understood. Roger that.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hah... Well, that's not good.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Sluggish, torpid... This body is a disappointment.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: I can barely muster... Tsk, ten percent of my original strength... You've ruined everything, again...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Let me guess... You didn't get a human body back, did you?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Hah... Urrgh... Raaaarghhh!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh! What's with him!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is bad! His presence feels completely different now... He's even stronger than before!)

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Vedrfolnir...! Rhinedottir...! Arrghh... Tholindis! Tholindis!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Watch out! Whatever rationality he still had when he was searching for his body is gone... All that's left is the calamity you see before you, a monster fueled by nothing but his own obsession!

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: It matters not... Having a heart... Being human... It's all irrelevant, completely and utterly insignificant!

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: You! You matter not... Nor does anything in this world! Gah! Argh, argh! None of it matters to me!

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Heh... Heh...

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: ...Fools. Time to die.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ugh... Aah...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: My strength... still isn't returning...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It seems my time... is running out...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It's getting late. The situation is urgent, but rest is vital. Good night, both of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're... We're safe?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It seems this young lady aided in our escape. You have my sincere gratitude, dear madame.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The flowers here bloom in such peaceful silence. I imagine you would not have invited anyone here, were it not an emergency.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh, talk about a good judge of character...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Oh? I take it that means you've been here before, then? In that case, I count myself fortunate to be your associate.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Columbinaaaa... What did you do that for!?!?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I studied his abilities inside-out... Equipped Pulonia with comprehensive countermeasures... We were going to settle the score...!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But he still broke through, did he not?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What, you expect a battle to be completely one-sided!?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I just... didn't expect him to have no sense of honor, whatsoever! Pulonia would have been fine in a head-on clash, but battles just... get chaotic...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh... So you actually thought you could win.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Have you been taking care of yourself lately? Your calculations seem to have deviated quite seriously. Perhaps you could try sleeping and rising earlier, or you could adopt my previous recommendation and—

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hey, listen here, Columbina! I tolerated your nonsense previously because we were colleagues.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: There's a Fatui warrant out on your head, and don't you forget that. Don't make me fight you right here and now.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, I was just a little concerned about you, that's all... Just like that time when you weren't making any progress with your research, so you went and cooped yourself up all alone...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That was none of your business! And don't you ever drag me out to one of your freaky hovels again!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Come on, Pulonia. We're leaving!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... W—Well, anyway, thank you!

choices.text: We would've been in a tight spot without you.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I was worried about you, too — not only because the remains of the Eternal Moon Goddess cannot fall into his hands, but also... because you've done much for me yourselves.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: And then I... Well, I brought your associate along for the ride, too. But that was as much as I could do.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: You're not afraid to speak your mind, miss — I like that. Please, call me Flins. It is my honor to make the acquaintance of one such as yourself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, what do we do now? Rerir's gotten stronger again. At this point, it doesn't seem like we can beat him.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: We did block most of the kuuvahki, so I'd say we've put a lid on his plans, for now at least.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But we still don't know what his aims are, and he may continue gathering power... So we must be very careful.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: After you left, I could no longer sense his presence...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means it's safe out there for now, right?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: A question, if I may, kind Miss Columbina.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: When the cannon's kuuvahki beam was deflected earlier, I saw several bolts of energy streak toward Hiisi Island, only to be blocked. Did you also have a hand in that?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: No.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I see... Curious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah. The cannon veered off course in the end, didn't it? Paimon wonders how Aino and the others are doing. Let's head back and check on them!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: In that case, Miss Columbina, I shall not disturb your serenity any longer. Thank you once again for coming to the rescue.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Go now, all of you. Do not worry.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you...

choices.text: This was quite unexpected.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A short while earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Remember these words: "The road shall be paved with truth, and we shall pave it ourselves."

dialogues.speaker: Follower A
dialogues.text: It's... It's you, Lady Moonchanter! It's her, everyone. It's her!

dialogues.speaker: Follower B
dialogues.text: You're right, my Lady. At times like these, we must rely on ourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit A
dialogues.text: We'll grab this, and this...

dialogues.speaker: Bandit B
dialogues.text: All of it's ours!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit A
dialogues.text: Hey! Something's wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit B
dialogues.text: Ugh, forget it, just run—!

dialogues.speaker: NPC#15457
dialogues.text: We won't let you pass!

dialogues.speaker: Follower A
dialogues.text: Leave this to us, Lady Moonchanter! Go!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit C
dialogues.text: I always knew something was off about you. You're actually some Abyssal creature, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Bandit D
dialogues.text: Time to teach you a lesson you won't forget!

dialogues.speaker: Follower B
dialogues.text: Please, calm down. They're clearly innocent!

dialogues.speaker: Victim A
dialogues.text: Thank you... Aaaagh!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit C
dialogues.text: You mind your own business!

dialogues.speaker: Kukka
dialogues.text: *sob* *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Person Fleeing A
dialogues.text: Ah! Someone help me!

dialogues.speaker: Person Fleeing B
dialogues.text: Run, run!

dialogues.speaker: Person Fleeing C
dialogues.text: Aaaahhh!

dialogues.speaker: Person Fleeing D
dialogues.text: This place is burning too!

dialogues.speaker: Person Fleeing E
dialogues.text: What are you waiting for!? Let's get outta here!

dialogues.speaker: Person Fleeing F
dialogues.text: I'm never coming back to this lousy place again!

dialogues.speaker: Person Fleeing G
dialogues.text: Move it! Outta my way!

dialogues.speaker: Suoma
dialogues.text: You wretched monsters! You're not getting anywhere near the cannon!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The monsters you fear do not exist here. The madness you have fallen to has been the source of untold disasters.

dialogues.speaker: Bartol
dialogues.text: You think we had a choice!?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: "Destiny" is no excuse for greed and destruction.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The choice has always been yours to make, and it remains so even now.
